canonical_question: Does the high wear and corrosion resistance of the CrMoNbWV alloy depend on the presence of the Ta2VO6 oxide phase?

question_variants.question: Does the high wear and corrosion resistance of the CrMoNbWV alloy depend on the presence of the Ta2VO6 oxide phase?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text mentions the presence of a Ta2VO6 oxide phase in a cited NbMoTaWVCr alloy (7.7% Laves, 6.2% Ta2VO6) but does not explicitly state that this specific oxide phase is the cause of the high wear and corrosion resistance of the CrMoNbWV alloy synthesized in the current paper. The current paper discusses wear/corrosion resistance generally but does not link it mechanistically to Ta2VO6. The cited work links high mechanical properties to solid solution and grain size, not specifically wear/corrosion via Ta2VO6.

answers.answer: The text states that in a cited NbMoTaWVCr alloy, the volume fraction of the oxide phase Ta2VO6 was 6.2%, and the Laves phase was 7.7%. However, the text attributes the high mechanical properties (yield strength) of that alloy to an interstitial solid solution and fine grains, not explicitly to the Ta2VO6 oxide phase for wear/corrosion resistance. The current paper discusses the corrosion current density of the CrMoNbWV alloy but does not link its resistance to the Ta2VO6 phase.
answers.conditions: room temperature, 0.5 M H2SO4 (implied for current paper context, though specific to cited work's mechanical testing)
answers.measurement_outcome: Oxide phase Ta2VO6 volume fraction: 6.2%; Yield strength: 3416 MPa.
answers.mechanism: High mechanical properties attributed to interstitial solid solution and fine grains, not explicitly to the oxide phase for corrosion resistance.
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit mechanistic link provided between Ta2VO6 presence and wear/corrosion resistance in the provided text.
evidence_spans: Nevertheless, in Reference [ [2] ], an NbMoTaWVCr alloy with an extremely high yield strength of 3416 MPa and good plasticity of 5.3% at room temperature was obtained.
Volume fractions of Laves phase (Cr,V) 2 (Ta,Nb) and oxide phase Ta 2 VO 6 in this alloy were 7.7% and 6.2%, respectively.
According to the authors, the high mechanical properties were achieved by forming an interstitial solid solution in the matrix and by fine grains (1.24 µm).
